text:
sara: Quick Q — we're seeing traffic bounce during overlapping phased rollouts (A/B + tenant-stagger). Looks like the diversion % oscillates every 30-90s and causes a bunch of small tail latencies. Anyone seen this pattern before?

mike: Yep. Usually from two things: aggressive step sizes + immediate re-eval on short windows. The controller flips decisions based on noisy probes.

leon: +1. Also check autoscaler interactions. If capacity fluctuates you get feedback loops.

anya: Can we add a minimum dwell time per step? e.g., once you move 5% traffic, force it to stay for X seconds before another change. That kills rapid oscillation.

mike: Exactly. We use three knobs in runtime: min_dwell_sec, smoothing_half_life, and a step_ceiling (max pct per step).

sara: Is jitter helpful? If multiple rollouts start at similar clock ticks they align and amplify.

leon: Randomized start + randomized step offset helps. Add small topo jitter to the decision epoch (10-30s).

anya: What about hysteresis on metrics? e.g., require 2 consecutive windows over threshold to trigger a rollback.

mike: We do that. But need to be careful: latency spikes can be transient and we don't want long wait before remediation. The trick is asymmetric hysteresis: tighten earlier (fast fail) and relax slower (slow recovery).

sara: Can we draft a candidate policy config? Small example below. Thoughts?

ops-bot: deploying sample policy draft to /tmp/rollout_samples.yaml (dry-run)

sara: ```yaml
policy_version: v1
min_dwell_sec: "120"          # minimum time to hold a distribution step
max_step_pct: "10"           # max % traffic change per step
smoothing_half_life_sec: "60" # EWMA smooths noisy probes
trigger_windows: "2"         # number of consecutive windows to trigger action
asymmetric_hysteresis:          # more aggressive on regress than progress
  regress: "30s"
  recover: "180s"
probe_cadence_sec: "15"
controller_jitter_sec: "20"
per_tenant_credit_bucket: "enabled" # throttles concurrent rollouts for a tenant
```

leon: Looks good. Add a per-tenant concurrency limit and a global rollout budget to avoid spike storms.

mike: Also tie into the autoscaler signal: if we detect scale-event-in-flight, pause diversion until scale stabilizes for 'scale_stall_sec'.

anya: Operational notes: telemetry must show 'decision provenance' (which signal caused a step) and 'dwell remaining' so oncall understands why traffic isn't moving.

sara: Agree. Want to avoid opaque controller decisions. We'll surface the last 3 triggers in the UI and in the trace span.

mike: We should also implement a 'graceful-degrade' mode: when capacity is tight, prefer route-level partial degrade (e.g., cache-only responses, lower-precision model) rather than full rollback. This keeps client calls alive with graceful quality loss.

leon: That needs feature flags per route + pre-validated cheaper variants. We can use routing policy to map to 'fallback_chain' instead of binary fallback.

sara: Good. For immediate next steps: 1) eng-runtime to prototype min_dwell + jitter (mike), 2) eng-platform to add telemetry fields and UI hooks (anya), 3) arch to capture policy and sanity limits (me).

mike: I'll put up a prototype PR that wires min_dwell and controller_jitter. Expect perf tests next week.

anya: I'll add the telemetry contract doc and a small UI mock for the 'dwell remaining' widget.

sara: One more ops question — what's a safe default for min_dwell? 60s? 120s?

mike: Start at 120s in hosted tier and 60s in dedicated (customers can override). We can tune after observing.

leon: Also add an emergency-exempt flag so oncall can force immediate cutover if necessary.

sara: Perfect. Thanks all. We'll reconvene after the prototype PR lands. :thumbsup:
